items.title: Show HN: Frugal Tokens – explore costs and usage across coding agents
items.why_it_matters: A new visual explorer tool called Frugal Tokens lets you analyze your Claude Code session costs, cache misses, and tool usage. Since you are actively building AI-ingest with Claude Code, this helps you see exactly which files or prompts are burning through your budget. This week, run the Frugal Tokens analyzer on your AI-ingest project directory to identify which files are causing the costliest cache misses.

items.title: Show HN: Flow – Claude Code CLI for feature planning → review/testing → merge
items.why_it_matters: Flow is a new CLI supervisor for Claude Code that automates the entire cycle of feature planning, git worktree creation, coding, verification, and merging. It was bootstrapped using itself and helps enforce clean git discipline, making it easier to manage your repository. This week, install Flow and use it to plan and scaffold the next feature for AI-ingest directly from your terminal.

items.title: Show HN: Csift – the missing tool to sift your Claude Code sessions
items.why_it_matters: Csift is a utility built to parse and recover Claude Code's session files, which is a lifesaver if Claude freezes, crashes, or accidentally deletes files during a long run. It helps you recover your state without burning through your 5-hour session limits. This week, install csift so you have a recovery plan ready the next time Claude Code gets stuck in a loop on your Supabase schema.

items.title: Show HN: Turning websites into micro CLIs for Claude Code to save on tokens
items.why_it_matters: A new tool called `oc` lets you turn any website into a micro CLI, allowing you to pipe web content directly into Claude Code to save on token costs. Instead of copy-pasting entire documentation pages, you can feed Claude only the exact context it needs. This week, install `oc` and use it to pipe a specific Supabase or Next.js documentation page directly into your next Claude Code prompt.

items.title: Claude Code adds new "concise" output style setting
items.why_it_matters: Anthropic added a new "concise" output style setting to Claude Code. This forces the agent to write shorter, more direct responses, which speeds up your build times and saves on output token costs. This week, run `claude config set output concise` in your terminal to instantly speed up your coding sessions.

items.title: Show HN: Budget Guard – a hard daily cap for your OpenAI/Anthropic bill
items.why_it_matters: Budget Guard is a lightweight tool that lets you set a hard daily spending cap on your OpenAI and Anthropic API bills. This prevents runaway costs when you let Claude Code run autonomously on complex tasks. This week, clone the repository and configure a daily safety limit on your Anthropic API key to protect your wallet while vibe coding.

items.title: Show HN: Yado – Claude Code and Codex on Your iPhone
items.why_it_matters: Yado is a new iOS app that lets you run Claude Code and Codex in a dedicated Fly.io Linux machine directly from your iPhone. It keeps your sessions running in the background and sends you a push notification when the AI finishes its turn. This week, sign up for the 7-day free trial of Yado to test committing a quick CSS fix to your AI-ingest repo while away from your laptop.
